 Deconstruct Launches ‘Oily Skin Tested’ Campaign Featuring Real Consumers Testing Serums
 by 
 MN4U Bureau 
 October 31, 2026 
 in 
 Campaigns 
 Reading Time: 2 mins read
 A 
 A 
 A 
 A 
 Reset 
 Share Share Share Share 
 Bengaluru: Deconstruct, the science-backed skincare brand built on its philosophy of “Highly Effective, Yet Gentle”, has launched ‘Oily Skin Tested’, a documentary-led campaign featuring real consumers comparing serum formulations on oily skin. The campaign aims to highlight the importance of choosing skincare formulations based not only on active ingredients and skin concerns but also on individual skin types.
 The initiative began with a question around whether serums marketed as suitable for all skin types are necessarily appropriate for oily skin. To explore this, Deconstruct invited consumers across South India to participate in a product-testing exercise. From over 6,000 registrations, 10 participants with oily skin were selected for a day-long experiment in Chennai.
 As part of the documentary, participants share their everyday skincare challenges, including concerns around heavy and sticky formulations and excess oil. They are then introduced to two unidentified serums, applied to opposite sides of their faces, and asked to evaluate them through three tests designed to replicate everyday skincare conditions.
 The first test examines absorption and stickiness through a feather-based demonstration conducted after three seconds of application. Participants observe that the side featuring Deconstruct’s serum remains clear of feathers. The second test focuses on sunscreen and makeup layering, comparing the residue left when sunscreen is applied over both formulations. Participants notice no visible residue on the Deconstruct side, while some residue appears on the other side.
 The third test, the Noon Heat Test, involves exposing participants to a temperature-controlled environment simulating afternoon heat. The results, supported by sebum meter readings, indicate comparatively lower oil levels on the side where Deconstruct’s serum was applied.
 The documentary concludes by highlighting Deconstruct’s Niacinamide Clearing Serum as a formulation developed for oily skin. One participant describes the experience, saying, “It felt watery. It felt light,” while another expresses surprise at finding a serum suited to their skin type.
 Malini Adapureddy 
 Speaking about the campaign, Malini Adapureddy, Founder and CEO, Deconstruct, said, “ Consumers today are increasingly aware of the ingredients needed to address concerns such as pigmentation, dark spots and dullness. However, how a serum feels on the skin is equally important, especially when consistent use is key to seeing results. With ‘Oily Skin Tested’, we wanted to move beyond conventional advertising and let real consumers experience our formulations firsthand. By documenting these experiences, we aim to build greater transparency and trust while reinforcing our belief that oily skin does not need fewer results, it needs the right formulation.” 
 The campaign features Deconstruct’s Niacinamide Clearing Serum, formulated with 5% Niacinamide and 2% Alpha Arbutin to address concerns such as dark spots, hyperpigmentation, dullness and tanning. With its lightweight, non-sticky texture and compatibility with everyday skincare routines, the product reflects the brand’s focus on developing formulations that address specific skin concerns while considering individual skin-type requirements.
 Conceptualised in-house, ‘Oily Skin Tested’ combines real-consumer experiences, product demonstrations and documentary-style storytelling. The film will be amplified across Deconstruct’s social media channels and digital platforms, extending the brand’s conversation around informed skincare choices and the importance of selecting formulations suited to individual skin types.
